extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, medical coders, clinical coding managers, clinicians, Medicare providers, health policy analysts, and stakeholders submitting public comments on CMS IPPS/LTCH PPS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria CMS uses to define, split, reassign, and designate ICD-10 diagnosis and procedure codes into MS-DRGs (including O.R. vs non-O.R. designations and CC/MCC severity levels) for the FY 2027 IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria to create subgroups in a base MS-DRG
rubrics_metrics.description: All five criteria must be met for a base MS-DRG to be split (or subdivided) by a CC subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five criteria (verbatim from the preamble) are: (1) at least 500 cases in the MCC subgroup, the CC subgroup, and in the without CC/MCC subgroup; (2) at least 5 percent of the cases are in the MCC subgroup, the CC subgroup, and in the without CC/MCC subgroup; (3) at least a 20 percent difference in average costs between the MCC subgroup and the CC subgroup and between the CC group and NonCC subgroup; (4) at least a $2,000 difference in average costs between the MCC subgroup and the with CC subgroup and between the CC subgroup and NonCC subgroup; and (5) at least a 3-percent reduction in cost variance, indicating that the proposed severity level splits increase the explanatory power of the base MS-DRG in capturing differences in expected cost between the proposed MS-DRG severity level splits by at least 3 percent and thus improve the overall accuracy of the IPPS payment system.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS-DRG grouping principle (clinical similarity and resource utilization)
rubrics_metrics.description: MS-DRGs are a classification system intended to group together diagnoses and procedures with similar clinical characteristics and utilization of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS seeks to identify sufficient sets of claims data with demonstrated clinical similarity when developing diagnosis related groups. Clinical coherence and similar resource consumption are primary drivers for grouping and for any restructuring proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define MS-DRG logic with explicit diagnosis and procedure code lists
rubrics_metrics.description: MS-DRG assignment logic must be defined by explicit lists of ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes and ICD-10-PCS procedure codes used to identify cases for an MS-DRG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing new or revised MS-DRGs, CMS identifies the specific diagnosis and procedure code lists to include in the GROUPER logic (example: reference to Table 6P.5a and 6P.5b listing 58 diagnosis codes and 689 procedure codes). Surgical hierarchy and procedure lists are documented and published for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: MDC case assignment logic and header clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Each MDC reflects a major organ system or etiology and has a list of ICD-10-CM diagnoses/conditions that correspond to that MDC; those listed diagnoses (and the header labels) inform resulting MS-DRG assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headers and lists must be clear and clinically appropriate (example: under MDC 25 CMS proposes removing the term 'SIGNIFICANT' from the header 'AND PRINCIPAL DIAGNOSIS OF SIGNIFICANT HIV RELATED CONDITION' because some listed codes do not describe a clinically significant HIV-related condition). CMS will review and revise lists and headers to avoid overlap and ensure clinical appropriateness; further changes will be discussed in future rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure reassignment review criteria for MS-DRGs 981–983 and 987–989
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS reviews procedures producing assignment to MS-DRGs 981–983 (Extensive O.R. Procedure Unrelated to Principal Diagnosis) and 987–989 (Non-Extensive O.R. Procedure Unrelated to Principal Diagnosis) on the basis of volume, by procedure, to determine if cases should be moved into the surgical MS-DRGs for the MDC into which the principal diagnosis falls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review uses: a frequency count of each major operative procedure code; cross-MDC comparisons by procedure code volume; examination of average costs and length of stay; assessment for shifts in treatment or reporting practice that would render current assignment illogical; and consideration of any external requests. Generally CMS moves only those procedure codes for which there is an adequate number of discharges to analyze.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating Room (O.R.) vs Non-O.R. procedure designation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures are designated as O.R. or non-O.R. (and as extensive vs non-extensive, or non-O.R. affecting vs not affecting MS-DRG) for purposes of MS-DRG assignment based on whether and how the presence of that procedure impacts grouping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating designation CMS considers: whether the procedure would typically require the resources of an operating room; whether it is extensive or non-extensive; and to which MS-DRGs the procedure should be assigned. Historical physician panels informed designations, but CMS now plans a comprehensive review leveraging ICD-10 claims detail, clinical advisors, MedPAR data, and consideration of resource utilization beyond physical room location. CMS may restructure designations and consider surgical approach subdivisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of new procedure codes based on predecessor/similar codes and public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: For newly finalized ICD-10-PCS procedure codes, CMS generally recommends an O.R. or non-O.R. designation based on the assignment of predecessor codes or similar codes and publishes proposed assignments for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed assignments for new codes are made available (e.g., Table 6B—New Procedure Codes) and are subject to public comment; CMS refers to predecessor code assignments and similar procedures when recommending designations and MS-DRG mappings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard for redesignating procedure codes (claims/data-driven requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses claims data, frequency of cases, and analysis of whether the procedure drives resource utilization to decide whether to redesignate a procedure code from non-O.R. to O.R. or to change its MS-DRG assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS examines MedPAR claims for cases reporting the code, looks for volume (number of cases), whether the procedure is the underlying driver of resource use, average costs and length-of-stay patterns, and variance. If data are sparse or the procedure is not the main driver in reported cases (examples: XW033DA—donislecel-jujn had no reported cases; XW0V3WA—AGN1 had few cases and when present was accompanied by other O.R. procedures), CMS may decline to redesignate pending more data; emerging technologies may be considered as part of broader future analyses of cell and gene therapies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping rules when O.R. procedures are present but principal diagnosis falls elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases that contain O.R. procedures will map to MS-DRGs 981–983 or 987–989 when they do not contain a principal diagnosis that corresponds to one of the MDCs to which that procedure is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of an O.R. procedure on a claim can trigger assignment to the 'procedure unrelated to principal diagnosis' MS-DRGs even if the procedure code itself is not explicitly assigned to those MS-DRGs' logic. CMS does not always need to reassign a procedure code into those groups for the mapping effect to occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: CC/MCC classification historic criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically, a diagnosis was classified as a substantial complication or comorbidity (CC) if, when present as a secondary condition with a specific principal diagnosis, it would cause an increase in length-of-stay by at least 1 day in at least 75 percent of the patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification into NonCC, CC, or MCC was accomplished using iterative evaluation of each diagnosis code's impact on resource use. This historic metric underpinned early CC lists, but CMS has since pursued comprehensive data-driven re-analyses with updated methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive CC/MCC analysis methodology and principles
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses a comprehensive analysis combining mathematical analysis of claims data and application of guiding principles to evaluate the impact of each diagnosis code when reported as a secondary diagnosis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process includes: mathematical measurement of impact on resource use (examples: analysis using FY 2018 MedPAR claims), application of a set of guiding principles (nine guiding principles referenced), public transparency including listening sessions and supplemental files, and iterative public comment. CMS may postpone adopting widespread severity reclassifications until methodology and clinical rationale are more fully explained and data/analysis are robust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors prompting CMS to consider moving procedure codes between O.R./non-O.R. groups
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS considers moving procedure codes between O.R. and non-O.R. groupings (or between MS-DRG groups) when claims data and other evidence indicate that current assignments are no longer clinically coherent or do not reflect resource utilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS looks for: sufficient procedure volume to analyze; trends or shifts in treatment practice or reporting practice; differences in average costs and lengths-of-stay that justify reassignment; and external requests. CMS also considers whether moving a procedure would improve clinical coherence or payment accuracy, but will not reassign without adequate data support.
